identity.operation: Read supported compressed ancillary metadata after IDAT through png_read_end.

coverage_witness.supported_behavior: Decompress supported zTXt or compressed iTXt metadata after IDAT while reading to IEND.
coverage_witness.required_setup: A build with the relevant compressed-text reader enabled, a valid PNG with such a chunk after IDAT, and a read sequence that reaches png_read_end.

context_facts.statement: The entry accepts fuzzer bytes as a PNG stream. It rejects inputs shorter than eight bytes or with a mismatched signature, then supplies the remaining bytes through user_read_data.
The harness creates read and info structures, reads pre-image information, updates it, reads rows over the reported passes and height, and reads trailing chunks into end_info_ptr.
The supplied recipe edits pnglibconf.dfa to disable STDIO, WARNING and WRITE, runs autoreconf and configure, builds libpng16.la, and links the C++ fuzzer against the static library and zlib.
The harness sets both CRC actions to PNG_CRC_QUIET_USE and conditionally enables PNG_IGNORE_ADLER32 when that macro exists.

png_read_info accepts a stream whose signature bytes were already consumed through png_set_sig_bytes, then dispatches pre-IDAT chunks, including iCCP, zTXt and iTXt when their respective read support macros are enabled.

evidence.dependency_reason: The target supplies the consumed-signature count and invokes png_read_info.

context_facts.statement: png_read_end also dispatches trailing iCCP, zTXt and iTXt chunks under their read support macros; the target passes a non-null end_info_ptr.

evidence.dependency_reason: The target creates the end info structure.
The target reaches png_read_end after row reading.

context_facts.statement: png_read_update_info initializes rows when PNG_FLAG_ROW_INIT is clear. A later png_start_read_image call with that flag set takes the duplicate-call png_app_error path. The harness calls the two functions in that order.

evidence.dependency_reason: The target calls png_read_update_info first.
The target later calls png_start_read_image.

context_facts.statement: Both versions of pngread.c supplied here have identical complete-unit hashes, so the duplicate-call contract shown in this continuation is unchanged across those versions. This fact alone does not establish the effect of png_app_error under the supplied build.
After updating info, the harness checks png_get_IHDR and returns on failure; it also returns when width times height exceeds its 100000000 threshold.
The source row reader consumes IDAT through png_read_IDAT_data and the harness invokes that row reader for each pass and row. This is an existing route for IDAT processing.

evidence.dependency_reason: The target invokes png_read_row in its pass and row loops.

context_facts.statement: If the supplied bytes end before a requested read length, the harness callback calls png_error. The harness has setjmp cleanup paths around reading and row processing.
The complete old harness contains no explicit assert invocation. Its existing checks include signature, allocation, IHDR, dimension and setjmp error gates.
The target is a C++ fuzz entry linked against the libpng static library and zlib.
The supplied recipe edits pnglibconf.dfa to disable STDIO, WARNING, and WRITE, then runs autoreconf, configure, and the library build. It supplies no additional configure option in these lines.
Inputs shorter than eight bytes or failing the PNG signature check return before libpng read object creation; the remaining bytes become the read callback's buffer.
The read callback copies requested bytes from BufState, advances its pointer and remaining count, and calls png_error if the request exceeds the remaining input.
The target sets quiet-use CRC handling for critical and ancillary chunks and enables PNG_IGNORE_ADLER32 only when that macro is defined.
The primary read sequence creates read and info objects, installs the buffer callback, marks eight signature bytes consumed, then calls png_read_info and png_read_update_info.

After updating info, the target allocates one row using png_get_rowbytes, obtains IHDR values, rejects dimensions whose product exceeds 100000000, sets interlace handling, reads each row for every pass, and calls png_read_end.
The target has setjmp recovery around reading and row processing; each recovery path invokes PNG_CLEANUP and returns zero.
PNG_CLEANUP frees the row, destroys the read structures, and nulls their pointers. The handler destructor also destroys remaining objects and deletes BufState.
The supplied source exposes read chunk handlers for iCCP, zTXt, and iTXt only under their respective PNG_READ_*_SUPPORTED gates.
ICC colorspace acceptance requires valid length, header, and tag table checks and returns zero when the colorspace is already invalid or any check fails.

An invalid colorspace clears the iCCP information flag and frees its profile. png_get_iCCP returns profile data only when that flag is set and all required output pointers are supplied; rejection of an invalid profile therefore does not itself establish loss of a supported accepted-profile behavior.

The supplied png_set_benign_errors implementation says its default treats png_benign_error as an error; passing a nonzero allowed value sets the benign-error and application-warning/error warning flags.
The read structure includes user chunk and decompressed-allocation limits when PNG_USER_LIMITS_SUPPORTED is enabled; the comments specify that zero means unlimited for each.

The complete target entry contains no explicit assert invocation or comparison of decoded output; its existing checks are the input gates, object-creation checks, setjmp recovery, IHDR availability check, and dimension limit.
The entry reads a PNG from fuzz input through image rows and calls png_read_end with a separate end_info_ptr. Post-IDAT metadata is within the requested read-to-end operation.

The entry requires at least eight input bytes with a PNG signature and rejects images when width × height exceeds 100,000,000; its callback consumes the remaining input bytes and reports an overread through png_error.

context_facts.statement: The complete old harness contains no assertion that post-IDAT compressed metadata was decompressed; its explicit checks cover signature and IHDR availability, and its error branches return zero.
The entry reads fuzzer supplied PNG bytes through image rows and then calls png_read_end with an end_info structure. This makes reading to the PNG end part of the target's operations.

The harness calls png_read_update_info, png_start_read_image, png_read_row for each row and pass, and png_read_end in that order. The supplied lines do not establish whether this sequence reaches a compressed ancillary handler after IDAT.
The harness does attempt an end read after the row loop, so its call list does not support a categorical claim that it stops before late chunks.
The entry requires at least eight input bytes and a matching PNG signature. Its read callback consumes the remaining fuzzer bytes and raises png_error if a requested read exceeds them.
The harness returns before row reading if png_get_IHDR fails or if height exceeds 100000000 / width for nonzero width.

The supplied recipe edits STDIO, WARNING, and WRITE options, runs autoreconf and configure, and links the fuzzer with libpng and zlib. These lines do not resolve the effective compressed ancillary read options.
png_app_error calls png_warning when PNG_FLAG_APP_ERRORS_WARN is set and png_error otherwise. The supplied evidence does not show the flag's state when the harness calls png_start_read_image.

evidence.dependency_reason: Identifies the harness call whose possible error path remains unresolved.

context_facts.statement: The complete harness has no assertion or check that compressed ancillary metadata after IDAT was decompressed. Its explicit content checks are the PNG signature and png_get_IHDR result; it also applies an image size gate.
